On pickup, the Workshop's Dynamic Rarity is set to Standard or Unusual at 50/50 (room/options in the top-level battery_pack data section); the roll is deferred to the next hand dealt, where RNG is in scope. The second and later triggers in the same day do not re-roll -- they deterministically toggle to the other option (wiki: 'Triggering this effect multiple times in a day will always switch to the other one'). The wiki's Locations line also names Darkroom, Hovel, Mechanarium, Toolshed, Trading Post and Clock Tower, every one of which exists in rooms.json; spawn_rooms omits them, so the pack is rarer here than published.

See tests/test_shops.py::test_coupon_book_reduces_price_by_1 and ::test_coupon_book_floors_at_0. Nothing is missing; implemented was flipped to true on the strength of those two tests.

MAIN EFFECT built: the choice is over the FOUR RARITY LEVELS, not which Mechanical Room to target -- the room is whichever Mechanical Room (Room.is_category('mechanical')) was just drafted while the wrench is held; Game.choose detects the trigger and parks Phase.WRENCH_PENDING (engine/effects/items/gear_wrench.py; Game.can_set_wrench_rarity/set_wrench_rarity). The permanent choice is recorded in GameState.permanent_rarity / GameConfig.permanent_rarity, a SAVE-scoped dict carried by env/multiday.py::DayChain the same way axed_rooms is (survives the attempt wrap; NOT in DayChain._CARRYOVER_KEYS, which is bool-only). decks.py::build_decks consults cfg.permanent_rarity for the day-start bucket; Game.reset seeds state.dynamic_rarity from the same dict right after, so decks.py::set_dynamic_rarity/inject_rooms/inject_rooms_undealt/apply_upgrade agree on a wrenched room's bucket the rest of the day. Two things deliberately NOT built: (1) the wiki's separate pickup side effect (Workshop + Boiler Room -> Standard, that day) needs rng inside special_items._on_pickup, which takes none -- the same constraint battery_pack.py works around via a deferred pending-trigger resolved at the next deal; gear_wrench.py's own module docstring names this as a tracked gap. (2) The wiki also says the Conservatory writes this same permanent rarity slot and can reset a wrench-set rarity; this sim's Conservatory (decks.reroll_random_rarities) is a random DAY-SCOPED reroll of three undealt cards -- each moved card routes through set_dynamic_rarity so state.dynamic_rarity stays consistent with it for the rest of the day, but the reroll never touches the permanent record, state.permanent_rarity/GameConfig.permanent_rarity -- a known, deliberately-unfixed divergence from the wiki, not remodelled here.

Rates, denominator, pity and pity_fail live on this record's lockpick effect and are read by special_items.py::_attempt_lockpick, which prefers the Pick Sound Amplifier when both tools are held; the door kinds match too (locks.py's DOOR_SECURITY is a separate segment kind no lockpick path touches). The rate ladder is indexed by state.special.lockpick_successes (successful picks today), matching "the chance goes down after a successful lockpick" / "after the first three successful lockpicks, remaining lockpicks have a 19/101 chance". state.special.lockpick_fails is the two-sided pity counter (+1/fail, -1/success): at >= pity it auto-succeeds and resets to -1; at <= pity_fail it auto-fails and resets to 1. The wiki gates the auto-fail case on lockpicking skill <= 20 -- lockpicking skill itself has no stat here (docs/experiments-design.md, permanent_lockpicking_skill), so this sim applies it unconditionally. NOT modelled: the per-door clause resetting the counter to 0 on a door already attempted (this sim tracks global per-day counters, not per-doorway, per _attempt_lockpick's docstring); the numerator bonus from lockpicking skill and its 98/101 cap; the wiki's !Garage high-luck spawn entry, which spawn_rooms_high_luck leaves empty; and its statement that building the Pick Sound Amplifier keeps this Kit out of the item pool on SUBSEQUENT days -- shops.py::fabricate marks recipe inputs consumed for the current day only.

Not a colour-bias mechanic. Owner ruling 2026-08-12, which overrides the wiki: drawing a Red Room while drafting offers the option to filter it from ALL draws for the rest of the day; the player may take this once per hand, unlimited hands, gaining 1 gem and redrawing each time. There is no exemption -- not for colour-selective drafts, the Silver Key, the Prism Key, or ducts; the wiki's claim that blocked rooms remain obtainable by those routes is wrong. Matched with Room.is_category('red'), which yields 18, NOT the 13 rooms whose category field literally equals 'red' -- the five Aquarium-family rooms count as every colour. The filter lives in draft.py::room_draftable (the single gate every draw path passes through), keyed off SpecialItemsState.crown_blocked_rooms; it is a draw-time exclusion, never a deck removal or move, so deck sizes and the rarities they make legal are untouched. SpecialItemsState.crown_block_used tracks the once-per-hand spend and resets whenever a hand is dealt or redealt (draft.py::_fill_options), so a redraw's fresh hand re-offers it. Game.can_crown_block/crown_block are the player-facing API; env/actions.py CROWN_BLOCK_BASE (376..378, one id per option slot) drives them, and item_state[11] reports the running blocked-room count. Reachability: the wiki says Room 46 ALWAYS contains this, so it is guaranteed_in room_46 rather than a spawn_rooms luck roll -- room_46 has additional_max 0 and is an area node travel_to reaches without ever calling roll_room_items. Granted by special_items.py::on_area_arrival, which reads guaranteed_by_room generically. The wiki's 'It cannot be obtained the first time the room is reached, but is present in other times' is modelled by engine/effects/items/crown_of_the_blueprints.py::gate on cfg.room46_reached -- day granularity, so a second arrival on the FIRST day still grants nothing; the same convention the eight Sanctum Keys already use for this flag.

The wiki describes three mechanically distinct File Cabinet Keys (Patio, Laundry Room, Tunnel), each opening its own drawer; only the Patio one is modeled, and it is the sole gate on upgrade_disk_archives (requires_item). Owner ruling: exactly one file_cabinet_key, obtained by digging the Patio's single dig spot (rooms.json patio.items.dig_guaranteed) -- a modeled stand-in for the wiki's actual, unmodeled mechanism (a hidden dig spot inside the Aquarium, reachable only after draining it via the Pump Room to water level <=1). The Laundry Room key (same unmodeled Aquarium-drain mechanism) and the Tunnel key (Crate Tunnel, out of scope by standing ruling) are not modeled.

meta.notes: DECIDED never to build, not blocked. It is the prize of the clock/castling puzzle in the Unknown, which no RL policy will learn to solve. Its payoff is already granted anyway: config.py sets royal_scepter_found True by default, deliberately, so the scepter is exercised as a game mechanic without the unlock chain. Genuinely absent -- no spawn room, no guaranteed source, and reachable only by injecting it through GameConfig.starting_items, which is a test backdoor rather than play.

Three chips exist. The Entrance Hall vase holds one, smashed with any item carrying the smash tag (wiki: 'a Sledge Hammer or equivalent'); the West Path holds one, dug with any dig_tool item; the third sits in the Blackbridge Grotto pedestal and is taken with TAKE_GROTTO_CHIP. All three respawn at their starting location the next day -- the first two via the entrance_vase_broken / outer_chip_dug day-start re-grants, the third because GameState.grotto_chip_taken is day-scoped with no carry-over. The three_microchips gate counts held chips plus the pedestal chip while it is in place (areas.json counts_flag), so two carried chips open the Orindian Ruins; taking the pedestal chip gives three held, which keeps that gate open and also lights the Apple Orchard sundial. Tier 2 and no_receive: giveable at the Trading Post and losable to the Lost & Found, never received.
Guaranteed pickup simplifies the Closed Exhibit security-timer puzzle.

Obtainable in-run only via the unmodeled Treasure Trove / Key of Aries puzzle; with royal_scepter_found carry-over flag it is granted at day start instead. Activation (color bias) and scepter_<color> category biases are modeled in PR2.

One unique disk per source so each is inherently one-time use. Granted by opening Vault box 304. Box stays open permanently (vault_key_304 stays in used_vault_keys); the disk returns daily to the open box until spent. Draw mechanism implemented (chunk 2); individual upgrade effects deferred (task 9).

Reserve stock item in the Commissary, restocked every day: an unspent disk drops overnight and is offered again, and the player pays the 15 gold each time (the cost is the throttle, making hoarding wasteful). Once spent it leaves the reserve stock permanently via collected_disks. Draw mechanism implemented (chunk 2); individual upgrade effects deferred (task 9).

One unique disk per source so each is inherently one-time use. Found in the Garage car trunk. The trunk re-locks every night (unlike the Vault boxes), so Car Keys are required on every open, not just the first; the disk inside returns daily until spent. Once spent, later trunk uses draw from the later_pool. Draw mechanism implemented (chunk 2); individual upgrade effects deferred (task 9).

One unique disk per source so each is inherently one-time use. Granted by lighting the Trading Post dynamite chamber. Chamber stays open (trading_post in lit_targets); the disk returns daily until spent. Draw mechanism implemented (chunk 2); individual upgrade effects deferred (task 9).

The 16th and only repeatably-OFFERED disk: 15 fixed locations plus this one exhaust the game's supply of 16. The wiki says 'Unlike the other Upgrade Disks, this disk can appear repeatedly' - the OFFER recurs, but the disk is unique, so once held the tier-5 trade falls through to its other outcomes.

meta.notes: Tomb: near candles grant upgrade_disk_tomb + 4 dice; far candles reveal Diary Key — both pairs modeled as one ignition event granting all three (simplification: two-step reveal collapsed to one). Diary Key is a REWARD of lighting the Tomb, not a prerequisite. Chapel: lighting the altar grants accumulated Keeper of Tithes coins (chapel_tithes counter, incremented each time the entry -1 coin penalty actually fires); the payout is resolved in engine/special_items.py light(). Trading Post fuse grants (Upgrade Disk + 40 coins) are wiki-documented; the secret room is collapsed to an immediate grant since it is not modeled. Freezer thaw is temporary/daily and not modeled. Mine South ("area": true): lighting the eight candlesticks inside the Abandoned Mine (South) permanently lowers the stairway to the Precipice (engine/game.py::_gate_ctx sets the "candlestick_stairway_lit" flag from state.special.lit_targets, gating both mine_south<->precipice edges in areas.json); it has no grants here because the Upgrade Disk sitting in the mine is a separate, ungated pickup already granted on arrival by engine/special_items.py::on_area_arrival — granting it again here would double-pay. mine_south has no rooms.json record (it is an area-graph node, not a draftable room), so it is the one target keyed by an area id instead of a room id; "area": true marks that. absent_targets lists rooms/areas the wiki mentions that are absent from both rooms.json and this targets table (mine_south graduated out of it once the area graph modeled the node). Apple Orchard ("area": true): the wiki says an ignition tool scorches the sundial's base, the layers turn, and placing three microchips in the revealed holder unlocks the Satellite Dish permanent addition; "requires_items" (a dict of item id -> minimum held count) extends the older count-1 requires_item to a multi-item requirement, gating engine/special_items.py can_light()/light(). Any tool in the tools list above lights it. The wiki says "an ignition tool" without naming one; an owner play-report named the Burning Glass, and the owner ruled to trust the wiki, so the Torch lights it too. It has no grants here: lighting it sets the permanent GameState.satellite_dish_unlocked flag directly in light() rather than through the grants list, the same shape as mine_south's candlestick_stairway_lit flag, because the reward is a config unlock, not an inventory item or resource. Not reachable in play today: the sundial demands three HELD microchips, but the engine's microchip ceiling is two (day_start/vase_smash/doorstep/doorstep_dig, see the microchip record's meta.notes) -- the third microchip always sits in the Blackbridge Grotto pedestal, counted by the three_microchips area gate's counts_flag without ever being carried, so it cannot also satisfy this held-in-hand requirement. Built correctly and left unreachable, the same deliberate state as the pre-#210 three_microchips gate before the pedestal chip was modelled; no new chip source was added to close the gap. requires_item (singular, count-1) is supported by the engine but no target uses it (the Diary Key is a reward of the Tomb, not a prerequisite); requires_items (plural) is used by apple_orchard only.

Telescope's own SpoilerBox ("another use"): "The Telescope can be used in the Planetarium to permanently upgrade the room, unlocking a planet that confers permanent benefits to the room. Doing this does not consume the Telescope, but only one upgrade can be done per day." Both the Telescope and Planetarium pages carry the same five-planet gallery, verbatim: "The planets seem to appear in a random order, except Mora which is always last... Once all five planets appear, the Telescope can no longer be used in the Planetarium." Payload kinds: 'container' (Dauja spawns a Trunk -- containers.rooms has no static Planetarium entry, so engine/special_items.py's _planetarium_container_kinds overlays this generically, the same per-room-overlay shape as the Entrance Hall's trunk count); 'dig_bonus' (Veia -- the wiki's own Dig spots page, "Creating dirt piles": "1 dig spot will permanently appear in the Planetarium when activating one of the planet's effects using the Telescope", read as this specific planet's payload given the gallery's own Dirt Pile caption; modeled as +1 into state.special.veia_dig_bonus at the Planetarium's cell, the same generic per-cell overlay the Cloister of Veia and spread_dig_spots already share); 'food'/'dice'/'item' (Fennmora/Mamora/Mora -- an Apple, a single Ivory Die [dice resource, not the 4-dice Experiments effect], and a Prism Key, applied through the ordinary grants vocabulary special_items.apply_grant_list already resolves for containers and mail packages). Every unlocked planet's payload re-applies every later day (rooms/planetarium.py's ON_PLACE/ON_ENTER hooks), matching "permanent benefits to the room"; the day a planet is FIRST unlocked, engine/special_items.py::use_telescope_in_planetarium applies that one payload immediately since the room's own ON_ENTER already fired earlier that day.
